rows.basis: Growth in gross 'Servers and network assets', 34,330M − 25,584M = 8,746M, against purchases of property and equipment of 31,186M (excluding finance lease principal). This counts all server growth, AI and non-AI, net of any disposals; management said the 2022 step-up in capex was 'largely due to building out our AI infrastructure', but gave no share.

Growth in gross 'Servers and network assets', 46,838M − 34,330M = 12,508M, against purchases of property and equipment of 27,045M. This counts all server growth, not only AI. It excludes buildings and construction in progress, which is the shell for the new data center architecture that supports both AI and non-AI workloads.

Growth in gross 'Servers and network assets', 68,397M − 46,838M = 21,559M, against purchases of property and equipment of 37,256M. This counts all server growth; Meta said the 2024 server growth included 'both AI and non-AI hardware'.

Growth in gross 'Servers and network assets', 98,040M − 68,397M = 29,643M, against purchases of property and equipment of 69,691M. Meta's own 72.22B capex figure, which includes finance lease principal, is not used. This counts all server growth: Meta said the majority of 2025 capex went to the core business, and its GPUs can serve generative AI and core AI alike. Construction in progress rose from 26.8B to 50.5B, which is the shell and is excluded.

Guidance for 2026 capex, including finance lease principal, is a total: 115–135B in January, 125–145B in April, then 130–145B in July 2026, 'to support our AI efforts and core business' and Meta Superintelligence Labs. That is the whole, not the AI part, so no amount is taken. Forward signals not in the pack: 131.05B of contractual commitments, mostly third-party cloud capacity, and about 103.77B of leases not yet commenced.
The MD&A says efforts include 'significant investments in AI initiatives' for recommendations, ad tools and generative AI features. No amount or share is given.
The MD&A repeats 'significant investments in AI initiatives'. No amount or share of the 64,960M of costs is attributed to AI.

Meta says the cost increase was 'mostly due to higher employee compensation and infrastructure costs related to research and development, including our AI initiatives', and that compensation growth came 'particularly' from AI talent. None of the 81,515M is quantified as AI.
The 2026 expense outlook cites infrastructure costs and a full year of compensation for 2025 AI hires, plus new hires 'particularly AI'. No AI amount is given.

Meta has no AI segment; Family of Apps (198,759M) and Reality Labs (2,207M) are not AI lines. Video generation tools reached a combined 10B revenue run rate in Q4 2025, and 'a meaningful percent' of ad revenue comes from campaigns using generative AI features. These are run rates and usage of ad tools, not fiscal-year AI revenue.
In Q3 2026, management said AI 'is going to become a meaningful source of revenue diversification over time', with no amount or timing.
